reports.title: Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: The Company has revised key guidance figures for fiscal 2026 as shown in the current guidance as follows:

Previous | Current
New store openings, net(1) | 30 to 33 | 30 to 31
Net sales | $4.70 to $4.72 billion | $4.70 to $4.72 billion
Comparable store sales increase / decrease | "-0.5% to 0.0%" | 0.2% to 0.4%
Gross margin | 29.8% to 30.0% | 29.8% to 30.0%
Adjusted EBITDA | $225 million to $235 million | $225 million to $229 million
Diluted adjusted earnings per share | $0.51 to $0.55 | $0.52 to $0.55
Capital expenditures (net of tenant improvement allowances) | $170 million | $170 million

desk.headline: Sales up 0.9% to $1.18bn and adjusted EPS $0.16, both slightly above estimates; comps back in positive territory, full-year comp outlook raised but EBITDA range trimmed

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted diluted (non-GAAP); GAAP diluted EPS $0.13 vs $0.12

other.label: Comparable store sales
other.change: first positive quarter after three declines

results: Net sales rose 0.9% to $1.18bn, helped by new stores and a 0.5% rise in same-store sales, partly offset by the 36 stores closed earlier in the year.
More shoppers came through the doors (transactions +2.4%), but they spent a little less per visit (basket -1.9%).
Gross margin slipped to 30.0% from 30.4% on promotions, higher freight costs and weaker produce demand after a Cyclospora food-safety outbreak.
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.16 from $0.21 and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $59.4m; GAAP profit rose to $13.3m thanks to $3.6m of net restructuring credits.
Capital spending fell to $28.1m (from $44.4m) as store openings slowed; total store-closure (Optimization Plan) costs are now estimated at $22–29m, a higher range than before.

guidance.summary: Grocery Outlet kept its fiscal 2026 sales range of $4.70–4.72bn and raised its same-store sales outlook to growth of 0.2–0.4%, but cut the top of its adjusted EBITDA range and tightened adjusted EPS to $0.52–0.55. It also now expects fewer new stores (30–31).

points: Management said more value-focused shoppers, squeezed by inflation, are responding to its pricing message, lifting store traffic.
The main lever is more 'opportunistic' (bargain closeout) products; some everyday lines were cut to make room in the supply chain.
Promotions are shifting from broad discounts to targeted events; an August 80th-anniversary event produced double-digit comps.
The produce outbreak hurt sales less than feared; repairs, occupancy and supply-chain costs remain a drag on expenses.
The CEO said the quarter was encouraging but there is 'much left to do' before the company is satisfied.
call.source: Call coverage: Grocery Dive (11 Nov 2026) and StockStory via Webull (Nov 2026); no prepared remarks filed

watch: Whether same-store sales keep growing in Q4 now that comps have turned positive.
Gross margin and EBITDA as targeted promotions, freight and store costs weigh on profit.
Completion and final cost of the store-closure plan, now expected to run into late fiscal 2027.
